subject: Banding Nexus: benchmark results and recommended geo tethering
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@compbench.co>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Banding Nexus deliverable: Q2 benchmarking package

Hi Hannah,

Attached is the Q2 benchmarking package we discussed: a market crosswalk across small- and mid-market SaaS comp data, localized geo indices, and a toy simulation that shows offer velocity impact at different top-of-band anchors. Highlights: 
- US West tends to sit ~3% above national midpoint for senior ICs in our comp family; UK/IE ~5% below midpoint but with higher variable prevalence.
- Overlap between L4/L5 in startups with heavy equity causes median compression; our sim shows that tightening overlap reduces acceptance at top-of-band by ~2.4 p.p.

Files: CompBench_Q2_bandbench.xlsx, geo-sim-anchoring.csv

Happy to walk through these with the team — happy to join a calibrations call if useful.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Analyst, CompBench Ltd.
Attachments: CompBench_Q2_bandbench.xlsx (spreadsheet), geo-sim-anchoring.csv (csv)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Banding Nexus deliverable: Q2 benchmarking package

Team — forwarding Aisha's package. Key asks from People Ops / Recruiting side: decide whether we adopt CompBench's suggested "geo tethering" adjustment (per-role multipliers anchored to midpoints, with a +/- band slope cap) and whether to pilot the tighter L4/L5 overlap reduction in the next 30 offers.

My read after a quick pass:
- The geo multipliers look conservative and tied to large samples; adopting them would increase near-term offer costs most in UK/IE and Brazil, but would reduce negotiation churn.
- The simulation shows fewer rescinds when we reduce L4/L5 overlap by 10%; risk is losing some top-tier hires who expect top-of-band offers.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick calibration session (45m) with Compensation + Recruiting to confirm anchor points — Laura to lead.
2) Pilot in Bay Area + Remote US West for 6 weeks on new tethering values; Marissa to track offer acceptance / velocity.
3) Legal/Finance to review any P&L signal before wide rollout (I can own the handoff).

Please review the attached annotated proposal I made (annotated-band-proposal.pdf) and tell me any immediate objections. If none, Laura, can you schedule the calibration this week?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Talent Strategy | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0102
Attachments: annotated-band-proposal.pdf

Thanks Hannah — quick thoughts before the cal session: 
- I ran a blind cross-check on our existing offer history (last 9 months) against the CompBench midpoints; the average deviation by role cluster is roughly +2.7% (we're slightly above market on average), but distribution is fat-tailed — a few roles in LATAM and UK are meaningfully below.
- I like the tethering approach but propose we: 
  a) Keep current band widths for leadership and sales comp-families; change applies to IC ladder only for now.
  b) Implement a soft cap: no single offer should exceed top-of-band + 8% without VP approval. That preserves escalation.

For the L4/L5 overlap reduction: I'm concerned about candidate perception for high-impact IC roles. Rather than compress overlap universally, let's run the pilot for 30 offers in Eng and ML only and evaluate. Metrics: acceptance rate, days-to-accept, and counteroffer incidence.

Scheduling: I can host calibration on July 20, 1:30pm PT. Sending invite.

Laura Bennett
Compensation Lead | Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-19T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Banding Nexus deliverable: Q2 benchmarking package

Appreciate the rapid work here. I'm on board with a conservative rollout:
- Pilot tethering for IC roles only (Eng + ML + Product) across US West and Remote US cohorts for 6 weeks.
- Approve the VP escalation guard (top-of-band + 8%).
- Headcount impact: Finance should model the worst-case uplift across active reqs for July/Aug and we will decide on reauthorization if uplift exceeds $300k incremental run-rate. Hannah, please loop Finance and send me the cost delta by 7/23.

One ask: include a short candidate communication note in the pilot (single-paragraph rationale) to keep managers consistent in offers. Marissa, can you draft?

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Talent & People Ops | Redwood Inference
